scenes.title: The Power of Polynomials
scenes.description: Introduce the challenge: complex functions like sin(x) or e^x are hard to calculate by hand. Polynomials are easy. How do we bridge the gap?

scenes.title: Matching at a Single Point
scenes.description: Step-by-step construction of the approximation. Start with f(a), then match slope f'(a), then curvature f''(a). Show how the polynomial 'hugs' the function better at each step.

scenes.title: The General Formula
scenes.description: Reveal the Taylor Series formula. Explain the factorial denominator and the (x-a)^n term visually.

scenes.title: Visualizing Convergence
scenes.description: Demonstrate with sin(x) or cos(x) around x=0. Show the interval of approximation growing as n increases.
visual_elements: Animation of sin(x) being approximated by 1st, 3rd, 5th order polynomials

scenes.title: Why This Matters
scenes.description: Summary of applications: calculators, physics simulations, and solving differential equations.

visualization.primary_visual: Split screen: Left side showing derivatives being calculated, Right side showing the polynomial curve morphing to fit the target function.

key_points: Any smooth function can be approximated by a polynomial
The approximation is exact at the expansion point a
Higher derivatives give information about higher order behavior
Factorials grow fast, ensuring convergence for many functions
educational.emphasis: The intuition that derivatives define the local shape, and summing them up reconstructs the global function.
